Username and password login. Two roles held on the user record: analyst
(submit) and reviewer (approve or override). No single sign-on — out of scope.

Order matters: rules first, then the LLM explains.
A duplicate is a database fact, not the model’s
opinion. The LLM turns those facts into a tier, a
rationale and a reviewer checklist — so the demo
Pydantic validates the form AND the LLM JSON.

DATA FLOW — follow the numbered arrows
Analyst signs in; token issued, carrying their role.
Fills the onboarding form. (Happens in the browser.)
Form posted to the API; fields and formats validated.
Screening Engine queries the vendors table for
duplicates: exact ABN · exact bank · partial match.
Findings + form go to the Gateway, which loads the prompt.
HTTPS call to Claude (system + user messages).
JSON reply validated, then written to the vendors row.
Result card shows tier, anomalies, verify list, rationale.
Reviewer approves, or overrides the tier and says why.
This is the human gate. Nothing self-approves.
Audit Logger records the AI decision and the override.
Vendor Master and Eval Log read back from the database
— so override rate is measurable from day one.
The only service outside this machine is the model API.
HTTPS · key read from .env · never committed
Hosting, storage and auth are all local: uvicorn serves the API, vite serves
the UI, SQLite is a file on disk, login is in-app. No queue — see below.
user: the vendor form + the rule findings
Every field returned is a field stored. Nothing is discarded.
FALLBACK PATH — when the model call fails
Trigger: timeout · rate limit · malformed or invalid JSON
Serve the rule findings on their own.
Banner: “AI summary unavailable — the checks below are
Status stays pending. Nothing is ever auto-approved.
The screen degrades. It never blanks.
a number on an arrow = data moving between components
a caption under a box = the step happens inside it
dashed = reading data back, not a new action
Heavy border = the three parts the live demo hinges on.
PK / FK = primary / foreign key · 1..N = one row links to many rows
SCOPE — WHAT IS NOT BUILT, AND WHY
· Sanctions screening. The brief names it, but Appendix A supplies no
watchlist. The reviewer checklist raises it as outstanding instead.
· Processes 1 and 2. Migrations still create invoices, purchase_orders
and budget_actuals, so the schema matches the brief.
· No SSO, mobile layouts, multi-tenancy, CI/CD or async queue.
A reviewer should get from clone to running app in four commands:
cp .env.example .env · alembic upgrade head · seed · run
Public repo, link shared at least 24 hours before the interview slot.
Migrations are repeatable — drop the file, re-run, reseed, same state.
DESIGN PRINCIPLES → WHERE THEY LIVE IN THIS DESIGN
The UI says “Approve vendor”, never an endpoint name. The default
state is the most common action, not the easiest one to code.
The tier is always overridable. The rationale sits beside every
recommendation. Every decision and every override is logged.
Prompts live in /prompts/, system + user pattern, JSON schema out.
The edge cases are already sitting in the seed data.
Loading and empty states throughout. One synchronous model call,
roughly two to four seconds, with the fallback path to its right.
Two checks built properly rather than three built thinly. Every
omission is a recorded decision, not an oversight.
FinanceOS technical assessment · Process 3 of 3 · every layer runs on the presenter’s machine · seed data: 25 vendors including 3 exact duplicates and 2 partial duplicates
